This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place, no matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
Many residents and tourists along the Gulf Coast of the Florida Panhandle and Alabama continue evacuating ahead of Hurricane Iseas.
The storm is expected to make landfall tonight or early tomorrow.
Currently, Iseas is a Category 2 hurricane with top sustained winds of 105 miles per hour.
In Mexico Beach, Florida, the locals say Iseas reminds them of another hurricane that hit their community eight years ago as a Category 5 storm.
Randy Vuckstoe with member station WFSU reports.
As Iseas continues to head towards landfall, Miles Magalski, Mexico Beach City Administrator, says community members are feeling nervous.
He says in years past a hurricane may have been excused for a party, but this time...
Because of Hurricane Michael now, I've not heard of one party being scheduled for this particular Friday night.
As of now, the storm is rejected to head north, making landfall somewhere between Pensacola and Alabama.
But many Mexico Beach residents say the path reminds them of what they saw with Michael.
Now they are preparing for the worst, setting up sandbags, grabbing supplies, and moving vehicles to higher ground.
For NPR News, I'm Randy Vuckstoe in Panama City, Florida.
Hurricane Michael caused billions of dollars worth of damage.
The Pentagon says December's execution of former U.S. Army Major Nidal Hassan will be live streamed.
Hassan is to be executed by firing squad for killing 13 people and injuring more than 30 others in an attack at Fort Hood, Texas.
The shooting at the base occurred in 2009.
Hassan's execution would be the first carried out by the military in more than 65 years.
The Department of Homeland Security says officers with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement were carrying out a targeted operation in New York City yesterday when a man was shot and wounded.
New York's police commissioner says the 28-year-old was shot inside a vehicle.
A 5-year-old was also in that vehicle. He was not injured.
Authorities in Russia say they've lifted all public health restrictions following the death of a 28-year-old lab worker at a plague research institute in Siberia.
As NPR's Charles Mains reports from Moscow, the woman's death has raised concerns about a potential outbreak of plague or some other deadly pathogen.
Ever since the death of a female lab technician in Russia's Irkutsk region last week,
Russian health authorities have insisted she succumbed to an unknown form of pneumonia rather than the plague.
Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobsov all but declared that version final.
Kobsov said the deceased lab technician had been vaccinated and was immune to the deadly pathogen she worked with.
He also said thousands of tests found no evidence of infection among other lab workers and that life in Irkutsk would be going back to normal.
The de facto declaration of an end to the investigation comes despite calls by the World Health Organization and the White House for more Russian transparency about the case.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
As Democratic Senator John Ossoff of Georgia faced off against Republican Congressman Mike Collins.
In their first debate, Ossoff blamed the war and tariffs for raising prices.
Under Mike Collins and Donald Trump, it costs more than ever to buy a tractor for your farm or to plant an acre of cotton.
Collins, a two-term member of the House, criticized Ossoff for supporting Biden-era policies that raised inflation in the U.S. economy.
Inflation remains above the Federal Reserve's annual target of 2 percent.
UPS says it's planning to hire tens of thousands of seasonal workers for the upcoming holiday season.
Marlon Hyde with member station WABE reports.
UPS package volume can nearly double during the holidays, its peak season. In preparation for it, the company is hiring 100,000 temporary employees nationwide to help out.
That's fewer than in prior years as it uses more artificial intelligence.
UPS says over two-thirds of its U.S. packages are being processed through automation-equipped buildings, up from a year ago.
The company is introducing new or enhanced automated facilities in Denver, St. Paul, Syracuse, and Portland.
Meanwhile, UPS continues to slim down by 30,000 workers this year to reduce operational costs.
For NPR News, I'm Marlon Hyde, in Atlanta.
I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington.
